Zero Transmission

By: Anina Peens | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Where are Eskom's cable theft hotspot and what is it like to be a land owner caught in the middle?

Unique Selling Point:
If an Eskom pylon is running across your property, life is not simple. Private land owners near Eskom hotspot, Emalahleni are at constant war with cable thieves, while the battling state utility cannot do much to change the situation.

Summary:
The Vulcan/Minerva electricity pylon line used to supply power to the greater East of Pretoria, Midrand and parts of Northern Johannesburg. But, sadly, there is only about 10km left of the line. Eskom switched off the line in February, but information leaked and cable thieves moved in. The line has not been switched on again and most of it has now been stolen. Life for land owners, caught in the middle, became an everyday war. Strangers enter and exit private properties, brazen, arrogant and not scared of getting caught. The question is, if Eskom knows about the problem, why is it doing nothing about it? Is the utility waiting for the line to collapse completely before they repair and reconnect it, or is it abandoning the line for the copper vultures to feast?

Further information:
Every weekend, it’s the same story. On Friday nights they cut, on Saturdays, they compile and on Sundays, they collect. This is cable theft on a different scale, happening in plain sight.
Frequently used corridors are carved out by criminals, on private property and the landowners are mere onlookers to the constant crime happening on their land.
Meet Martie Koegelenberg; a mother of two and farmer near Balmoral in Gauteng. Her life changed in February 2022 when the war against the cable syndicates started. A war to save
one of Eskom’s most important distribution lines. But the battle seems to be lost and Eskom is looking the other way.
The 400kvh Vulcan line is 80km long and built to provide electricity to the greater East of Pretoria. It is a brand new power line but there is nothing left of it. In February 2022, Eskom switched off the line to perform maintenance. That same day, the cable thieves struck. The main artery of the line was cut and the line was never switched on again. It has taken the criminals seven months to steal 60 km of the line. Now, they are returning to remove the steel from what is left of the structures.
While this was happening, Martie called out for help to the authorities multiple times. The Police did nothing and private security could not do much to assist the land owners in protecting them, their land or Eskom’s infrastructure. a Network of farmers was formed and 13 cable thieves were arrested in March, only to be released from custody three days later. All 13 criminals struck again.
Desperate for help, Martie wrote to Andre De Ruyter. And Andre phoned her, spending two hours on the phone to gather information. 50 Security vehicles were deployed to the area at a monthly cost of over 500 million Rand. But it didn’t help. Patrolling on farms is a different story than patrolling in the city. Eskom later said, the security bill was too high and withdrew the vehicles, leaving only three to patrol the 80km line. De Ruyter instructed high level meetings between local Eskom management and farmers at the Kusile power station. Ideas were exchanged and Eskom undertook to work with the farmers and private security to protect the line. But that was the last of it. Eskom never responded to reports again. And it seems that there could be a leak between Eskom and the criminals, because they know all too well that nothing is being done.
The ripple effect of this problem is massive. Farmers are too scared to work their land because strangers are constantly moving in and out of their gates. When they are cut cables exceeding 100 meters and massively heavy are dropped onto the farm land making it impossible for farmers to work their land. And Eskom never comes out to collect the cables.
Despite more attempts made to get Eskom to respond, again, directly to Andre De Ruyter seem to have fallen on death ears.

Treatment idea:
- It is Friday night and Martie and her children are having dinner in their house. We hear the two way radio alerts come through.. Martie tells her children to get ready for the night, they check all the doors and windows… in the passage, our presenter introducing the night on the farm…
- Then we take a trip with Martie to the hotspots and see what we can find.
- The next day we visit the same hotspots and go to the place where the first cable was chopped in March.
- We visit the local Eskom office, where no one is working from their offices…
- We speak to Eskom, preferably ADR. Who is responsible here?
- Energy expert: explanatory: just how much is 400KVA? Is this problem contributing to loadshedding in the city?

Additional elements:
• Land owners also suffer massive losses as the criminals’ open access to the farms lead to extended crimes: they steal anything they can find while making their way to the power line: they steal solar systems, pumps, vehicles ect.
• Baldwin is planning on building 600 thousand cost low income houses on land in the middle of this mess. The Vulcan line was supposed to supply power to this development.
• The Maputo corridor, which is under construction, is also supposed to get power supply from the Vulcan line.


Extra Budget Items:
One night accommodation for four people near the farm in Balmoral.

Traveling expense: Johannesburg-Balmoral and Balmoral-Johannesburg.

DRAFT 15: ZERO_TRANSMISSSION


TIMELAPSE SHOT OF SUNSET THEN MOVE TO HOUSE
NO MUSIC… JUST NIGHT NOISES
CAN MAYBE MIX IN RADIO IN BACKGROUND
MARTIE CLOSING WINDOWS AND LOCKING DOORS

VO
It’s early evening on a farm in Balmoral, East of Pretoria.

BREATHE

Martie Humphries and her husband live here with their two children, although he spends much of his time working abroad.

PAUSE

VO
In this isolated rural area, thoughts turn to safety when the sun sets.

SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER NO STRAP
MASA: So, now your doors are locked Martie, but are you ever really safe on a farm?
“I don’t think you are ever really safe, but it is a choice you make to stay here”

BREATHE
VO
For Martie and her neighbours, crime hasn’t always been a problem in this area.

SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER STRAP
“It used to be very quiet here, so we did not have worries about people walking around or stuff happening at night but lately it is not like that anymore”

VO
Since February, they’ve been living on a knife’s edge: when night falls, cable theft syndicates targeting two major power lines are on the prowl.

SHOT OF CUT FENCE AND SPOT LIGHT IN THE NIGHT? EK DINK ONS MOET MAAR DIE CUTAWAYS VAN DIE BAKKIE IN DIE NAG WYS- WAT ONS GEBRUIK HET VIR DIE REENACTMENT.

VO
The criminals scout during the day. They return at night, cutting through fences to get onto private property.

PAUSE

VO
The intruders are armed and dangerous, the landowners trying to protect the transmission lines running through their properties tell us. There’ve been several shootouts.

PAUSE

SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER
“We have never had any trouble with these lines and all of a sudden they have just been chopping it up, every week, every night”

VO
When we meet her and her boys, Martie’s husband has just returned from another stint abroad. But, for much of the past two years, it’s been just the three of them. We’re there at night - when Martie is at her most anxious.

PAUSE

VO
The next day, she shows us where the syndicate has been operating over the past eight months.


SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER
“Those pylons that you can see there, they are still on my property, the next one is the neighbors…”

VO
The pylons are the large steel structures carrying the cables. They’re spaced around 250 meters apart.

SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER
“So the cables that you see in the middle, there was a set of those cables running on this side of the pylon and there was a set that was running on that side…
MASA: Oh my word
“So, it is only the sensor cables that is left”

VO
Overhead power lines are Eskom’s electricity highways. Once they reach cities, they split into smaller lines, just like a network of roads connecting to freeways. The Vulcan/Minerva line runs parallel to the Duvha/Apollo line for around 80km from the greater Emalahleni area to Gauteng. While both these lines are targeted, Vulcan Minerva runs through Martie’s property.

SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER
MASA: This was an 80km line, do you know how much is left of it now?
“Of the 80 km I will guess ten is left”

SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER
MASA: This is not child splay stuff, they must know that its off though”
“Yes, this was switched off in February for maintenance and somehow it leaked that the whole line is off”


MASA WALKING NEXT TO LINE, TOUCHING IT
VO
Vulcan Minerva is a 400 KV power line. That means it can transmit up to 400 thousand Volts of live electricity.

SHOT OF MASA NEAR LINE AGAIN

LINK
“Now, under normal circumstances, I wouldn’t be able to touch or even step on an extremely high voltage cable like this…but here we find ourselves.

VO
Switched on, it’d be impossible to come within 12 meters of a power line of this size. But when it’s switched off, as it is now, cable theft syndicates have a field day, stripping the lines and cutting them into pieces. They’re after the aluminum that transmits our electricity.

SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS
“They work in big groups. So, its basically ten, fifteen minutes they cut it into pieces”

VO
Wian Lambrechts lives a couple of kilometers from Martie.
Two weeks before our visit, he heard a line falling from the pylon close to his farmhouse. He tried to track the criminals but they got away, leaving part of their loot behind.


SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS
MASA: Here we are, is this the crime scene?
“Ja this is where we found the cables you just saw now. And if you look back it is basically on our backdoor”

UPSOUND
SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS NO STRAP
“They cut it with equipment and then they take this aluminum pieces off and then you will see, right in the middle, there is a small piece, a steel cable.
MASA: Oh, that’s how they do it?
“The steel cable holds the lines, so they take off all the aluminum and they just leave the steel cable”.

VO
Since February, landowners like Martie and Wian have been risking their lives trying to catch the cutters.

PAUSE
STRAP: DRAMATISATION

The community gives us a demonstration of how they’ve organized themselves into a security watch – connected to each other by a radio system. When someone is seen lurking in the dark, the farm watch receives an alert. Moving quickly to an agreed location, they strategise, split into groups, and begin their search.

PAUSE

This is the stash left behind by the criminals Wian chased from his farm. Weighing close to a ton, it would fetch around 25 thousand Rand on the black market. Dozens of piles like this are often stolen in one go.

PAUSE
But it’s the tools found on the scene that raise arguably the most serious question.

SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS
“We got their equipment that they use”
MASA: Yes, it cant be that easy to chop it up”
“I want to show you this. So, these are basically equipment that you can buy in a local store, but these is very interesting, because this is basically Eskom equipment”

VO
In March, Wian and the farm watch successfully trapped a group of 13 suspects, who were then arrested by the police. They were carrying similar tools.

BACK TO BACK
SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS
“From their passports we could see that all of them are Mozambican people”
SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS
“They told us that they were instructed to take this package, to Johannesburg”

VO
Landowners are convinced that Eskom employees are part of the syndicate, responsible for training the cutters.
PAUSE
After the March arrests, Eskom deployed security to protect the lines.

INSERT LINK
“Behind me is a security vehicle, tasked with manning this massive power line. It’s almost like it’s a losing battle this”


SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER
“Eskom did get security guards in, a whole lot of patrol bakkies patrolling the area. They were here for about a month and then we didn’t see them again. I found out that the contract have been cut down to only three vehicles in this whole area, patrolling an 80km line”

VO
Martie complained to Eskom about the lack of security but says nothing came of it. The landowners claim they’re fighting a lone battle, but Eskom disagrees.

SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM
“We are certainly aware of the activity in that area, and we are driving intelligence-led investigations there”

VO
It an uphill battle for Eskom group head of security, Karen Pillay, tasked with strategizing on how to protect the utility’s more than 400 thousand kilometers of overhead lines.

SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM
“It is a matter of national interest in this point in time because it literally impacts a large scale of infrastructure across the country”

VO
But, according to Martie and other landowners, it seems the sense of urgency at Eskom’s headquarters isn’t shared by its employees in Mpumalanga. They claim local Eskom workers are turning a blind eye to the situation. When Wian found the stash of cables on his farm, he immediately alerted Eskom but no one responded. Pillay, though, says their plan is working

SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM
“ In the past three months we have seen at least a 40% reduction of incidents on that line so it can tell you that the interventions that we are driving are actually paying off”

VO
And Pillay’s adamant there’s sufficient security on the Vulcan/Minerva line.

SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM
“Security has not been withdrawn on that line”
MASA: But it was drastically withdrawn
“I would not necessarily say that because it’s essentially we have increased our security measures on that line including the manpower that we were deploying in that area”

VO
We only saw two patrol vehicles during our visit.

PAUSE

Crucially, Eskom doesn’t deny that its employees may be involved.

SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM
“We have been looking at the insider threat. We don’t discount the potential of that threat.
“Bear in mind that lots of information around Eskom is actually public information an especially around the transparency we maintain on the state of the system in particular”


VO
A day after our visit to Balmoral, the criminals were back and three days after that, again. Near the pylons that still had something left to steal, farmland was torched.
STRAP: CELLPHONE FOOTAGE
Farmers fought the flames throughout the night, and the next day, it was set alight, again. For Martie, it’s a nightmare she just wants to end.

SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER
“Now, we are hoping that they will take the whole line and move on to something else”

SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM
“We’re not dragging our feet about this, this infrastructure is critical, critical to Eskom and critical to the country”

VO
STRAP: CELLPHONE FOOTAGE OVER ESKOM PICKUP TRUCK
After our visit to Megawatt Park, Eskom finally fetched the cables from Wian’s farm and Pillay agreed that closer cooperation was needed with the landowners in the area. An urgent meeting was called but… Eskom’s middle management was unavailable… again.

LINK
“Even if Eskom solves its generation problem, how are they gonna adequately supply electricity if cable theft continues to flourish as it is here”

VO
If a powerline has zero transmission, its load is carried by an alternative line. But if the theft continues more lines will inevitably drop, causing blackouts that can’t be fixed overnight.



PROMOS

TUESDAY PROMO

MASA
“Even if Eskom solved its generation problems another problem will be transmission. Because how will it be able to distribute electricity if this is the state of its power lines”

“Considering all the loadshedding that we’re experiencing, it is very upsetting to see cables stripped like this. But what is even more upsetting? These criminals will come back”


SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM NO STRAP
“We have seen the groups that actually target the line, they are in excess of 20 to 30 people at a time”

ESTABLISH KAREN VISUALLY AT MEGAWATT PARK
VO
It is an uphill battle for Eskom group head of security, Karen Pillay, tasked with strategizing how to prevent the utility’s more than 400 thousand kilometers of overhead cables from being stripped. This crime is spiraling out of control

SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM PLEASE STRAP
“It is a crime that we actually see literally moving at a rapid pace. The moment you place interventions in a specific place, they will find another target area to move to”































PROMO 1
VO
Its an ongoing war as criminals enter and exit private property to strip Eskom’s power lines.
SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS
“We set a trap just next to our fence cause that is the road they use and to our surprise the next morning, we caught the vehicle standing next to the road with twelve people inside…”
VO
Landowners in Mpumalanga are at wits end, trying to fight against the syndicates.


PROMO 2
MASA
“Considering all the loadshedding that we’re experiencing, it is very upsetting to see cables stripped like this”
VO
A crime that is spiraling out of control. Cable theft syndicates slam down on some of Eskom’s most significant power lines. It seems to be a losing battle that affects the entire country.


PROMO 3
SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS
MASA: Where do those cables come from. argh I’m even… I am too scared to touch this. I don’t understand how they do it.
VO
If this cable was on, one would not come this close. But highly skilled cable theft syndicates have chopped it to pieces. How will Eskom win this war?

SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER NO STRAP MASA: So, now your doors are locked Martie, but are you ever really safe on a farm? “I don’t think you are ever really safe, but it is a choice you make to stay here” BREATHE VO For Martie and her neighbours, crime hasn’t always been a problem in this area. SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER STRAP “It used to be very quiet here, so we did not have worries about people walking around or stuff happening at night but lately it is not like that anymore” VO Since February, they’ve been living on a knife’s edge: when night falls, cable theft syndicates targeting two major power lines are on the prowl. SHOT OF CUT FENCE AND SPOT LIGHT IN THE NIGHT? EK DINK ONS MOET MAAR DIE CUTAWAYS VAN DIE BAKKIE IN DIE NAG WYS- WAT ONS GEBRUIK HET VIR DIE REENACTMENT. VO The criminals scout during the day. They return at night, cutting through fences to get onto private property. PAUSE VO The intruders are armed and dangerous, the landowners trying to protect the transmission lines running through their properties tell us. There’ve been several shootouts. PAUSE SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER “We have never had any trouble with these lines and all of a sudden they have just been chopping it up, every week, every night” VO When we meet her and her boys, Martie’s husband has just returned from another stint abroad. But, for much of the past two years, it’s been just the three of them. We’re there at night - when Martie is at her most anxious. PAUSE VO The next day, she shows us where the syndicate has been operating over the past eight months. SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER “Those pylons that you can see there, they are still on my property, the next one is the neighbors…” VO The pylons are the large steel structures carrying the cables. They’re spaced around 250 meters apart. SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER “So the cables that you see in the middle, there was a set of those cables running on this side of the pylon and there was a set that was running on that side… MASA: Oh my word “So, it is only the sensor cables that is left” VO Overhead power lines are Eskom’s electricity highways. Once they reach cities, they split into smaller lines, just like a network of roads connecting to freeways. The Vulcan/Minerva line runs parallel to the Duvha/Apollo line for around 80km from the greater Emalahleni area to Gauteng. While both these lines are targeted, Vulcan Minerva runs through Martie’s property. SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER MASA: This was an 80km line, do you know how much is left of it now? “Of the 80 km I will guess ten is left” SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER MASA: This is not child splay stuff, they must know that its off though” “Yes, this was switched off in February for maintenance and somehow it leaked that the whole line is off” MASA WALKING NEXT TO LINE, TOUCHING IT VO Vulcan Minerva is a 400 KV power line. That means it can transmit up to 400 thousand Volts of live electricity. SHOT OF MASA NEAR LINE AGAIN LINK “Now, under normal circumstances, I wouldn’t be able to touch or even step on an extremely high voltage cable like this…but here we find ourselves. VO Switched on, it’d be impossible to come within 12 meters of a power line of this size. But when it’s switched off, as it is now, cable theft syndicates have a field day, stripping the lines and cutting them into pieces. They’re after the aluminum that transmits our electricity. SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS “They work in big groups. So, its basically ten, fifteen minutes they cut it into pieces” VO Wian Lambrechts lives a couple of kilometers from Martie. Two weeks before our visit, he heard a line falling from the pylon close to his farmhouse. He tried to track the criminals but they got away, leaving part of their loot behind. SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS MASA: Here we are, is this the crime scene? “Ja this is where we found the cables you just saw now. And if you look back it is basically on our backdoor” UPSOUND SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS NO STRAP “They cut it with equipment and then they take this aluminum pieces off and then you will see, right in the middle, there is a small piece, a steel cable. MASA: Oh, that’s how they do it? “The steel cable holds the lines, so they take off all the aluminum and they just leave the steel cable”. VO Since February, landowners like Martie and Wian have been risking their lives trying to catch the cutters. PAUSE STRAP: DRAMATISATION The community gives us a demonstration of how they’ve organized themselves into a security watch – connected to each other by a radio system. When someone is seen lurking in the dark, the farm watch receives an alert. Moving quickly to an agreed location, they strategise, split into groups, and begin their search. PAUSE This is the stash left behind by the criminals Wian chased from his farm. Weighing close to a ton, it would fetch around 25 thousand Rand on the black market. Dozens of piles like this are often stolen in one go. PAUSE But it’s the tools found on the scene that raise arguably the most serious question. SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS “We got their equipment that they use” MASA: Yes, it cant be that easy to chop it up” “I want to show you this. So, these are basically equipment that you can buy in a local store, but these is very interesting, because this is basically Eskom equipment” VO In March, Wian and the farm watch successfully trapped a group of 13 suspects, who were then arrested by the police. They were carrying similar tools. BACK TO BACK SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS “From their passports we could see that all of them are Mozambican people” SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS “They told us that they were instructed to take this package, to Johannesburg” VO Landowners are convinced that Eskom employees are part of the syndicate, responsible for training the cutters. PAUSE After the March arrests, Eskom deployed security to protect the lines. INSERT LINK “Behind me is a security vehicle, tasked with manning this massive power line. It’s almost like it’s a losing battle this” SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER “Eskom did get security guards in, a whole lot of patrol bakkies patrolling the area. They were here for about a month and then we didn’t see them again. I found out that the contract have been cut down to only three vehicles in this whole area, patrolling an 80km line” VO Martie complained to Eskom about the lack of security but says nothing came of it. The landowners claim they’re fighting a lone battle, but Eskom disagrees. SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM “We are certainly aware of the activity in that area, and we are driving intelligence-led investigations there” VO It an uphill battle for Eskom group head of security, Karen Pillay, tasked with strategizing on how to protect the utility’s more than 400 thousand kilometers of overhead lines. SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM “It is a matter of national interest in this point in time because it literally impacts a large scale of infrastructure across the country” VO But, according to Martie and other landowners, it seems the sense of urgency at Eskom’s headquarters isn’t shared by its employees in Mpumalanga. They claim local Eskom workers are turning a blind eye to the situation. When Wian found the stash of cables on his farm, he immediately alerted Eskom but no one responded. Pillay, though, says their plan is working SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM “ In the past three months we have seen at least a 40% reduction of incidents on that line so it can tell you that the interventions that we are driving are actually paying off” VO And Pillay’s adamant there’s sufficient security on the Vulcan/Minerva line. SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM “Security has not been withdrawn on that line” MASA: But it was drastically withdrawn “I would not necessarily say that because it’s essentially we have increased our security measures on that line including the manpower that we were deploying in that area” VO We only saw two patrol vehicles during our visit. PAUSE Crucially, Eskom doesn’t deny that its employees may be involved. SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM “We have been looking at the insider threat. We don’t discount the potential of that threat. “Bear in mind that lots of information around Eskom is actually public information an especially around the transparency we maintain on the state of the system in particular” VO A day after our visit to Balmoral, the criminals were back and three days after that, again. Near the pylons that still had something left to steal, farmland was torched. STRAP: CELLPHONE FOOTAGE Farmers fought the flames throughout the night, and the next day, it was set alight, again. For Martie, it’s a nightmare she just wants to end. SUPER@ MARTIE HUMPHRIES: LANDOWNER “Now, we are hoping that they will take the whole line and move on to something else” SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM “We’re not dragging our feet about this, this infrastructure is critical, critical to Eskom and critical to the country” VO STRAP: CELLPHONE FOOTAGE OVER ESKOM PICKUP TRUCK After our visit to Megawatt Park, Eskom finally fetched the cables from Wian’s farm and Pillay agreed that closer cooperation was needed with the landowners in the area. An urgent meeting was called but… Eskom’s middle management was unavailable… again. LINK “Even if Eskom solves its generation problem, how are they gonna adequately supply electricity if cable theft continues to flourish as it is here” VO If a powerline has zero transmission, its load is carried by an alternative line. But if the theft continues more lines will inevitably drop, causing blackouts that can’t be fixed overnight. PROMOS TUESDAY PROMO MASA “Even if Eskom solved its generation problems another problem will be transmission. Because how will it be able to distribute electricity if this is the state of its power lines” “Considering all the loadshedding that we’re experiencing, it is very upsetting to see cables stripped like this. But what is even more upsetting? These criminals will come back” SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM NO STRAP “We have seen the groups that actually target the line, they are in excess of 20 to 30 people at a time” ESTABLISH KAREN VISUALLY AT MEGAWATT PARK VO It is an uphill battle for Eskom group head of security, Karen Pillay, tasked with strategizing how to prevent the utility’s more than 400 thousand kilometers of overhead cables from being stripped. This crime is spiraling out of control SUPER@ ADV. KAREN PILLAY: HEAD OF SECURITY: ESKOM PLEASE STRAP “It is a crime that we actually see literally moving at a rapid pace. The moment you place interventions in a specific place, they will find another target area to move to” PROMO 1 VO Its an ongoing war as criminals enter and exit private property to strip Eskom’s power lines. SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS “We set a trap just next to our fence cause that is the road they use and to our surprise the next morning, we caught the vehicle standing next to the road with twelve people inside…” VO Landowners in Mpumalanga are at wits end, trying to fight against the syndicates. PROMO 2 MASA “Considering all the loadshedding that we’re experiencing, it is very upsetting to see cables stripped like this” VO A crime that is spiraling out of control. Cable theft syndicates slam down on some of Eskom’s most significant power lines. It seems to be a losing battle that affects the entire country. PROMO 3 SUPER@ WIAN LAMBRECHTS MASA: Where do those cables come from. argh I’m even… I am too scared to touch this. I don’t understand how they do it. VO If this cable was on, one would not come this close. But highly skilled cable theft syndicates have chopped it to pieces. How will Eskom win this war?

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Where are Eskom's cable theft hotspot and what is it like to be a land owner caught in the middle?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: If an Eskom pylon is running across your property, life is not simple. Private land owners near Eskom hotspot, Emalahleni are at constant war with cable thieves, while the battling state utility cannot do much to change the situation.
metadata.Summary: The Vulcan/Minerva electricity pylon line used to supply power to the greater East of Pretoria, Midrand and parts of Northern Johannesburg. But, sadly, there is only about 10km left of the line. Eskom switched off the line in February, but information leaked and cable thieves moved in. The line has not been switched on again and most of it has now been stolen. Life for land owners, caught in the middle, became an everyday war. Strangers enter and exit private properties, brazen, arrogant and not scared of getting caught. The question is, if Eskom knows about the problem, why is it doing nothing about it? Is the utility waiting for the line to collapse completely before they repair and reconnect it, or is it abandoning the line for the copper vultures to feast?
metadata.Further information: Every weekend, it’s the same story. On Friday nights they cut, on Saturdays, they compile and on Sundays, they collect. This is cable theft on a different scale, happening in plain sight. Frequently used corridors are carved out by criminals, on private property and the landowners are mere onlookers to the constant crime happening on their land. Meet Martie Koegelenberg; a mother of two and farmer near Balmoral in Gauteng. Her life changed in February 2022 when the war against the cable syndicates started. A war to save one of Eskom’s most important distribution lines. But the battle seems to be lost and Eskom is looking the other way. The 400kvh Vulcan line is 80km long and built to provide electricity to the greater East of Pretoria. It is a brand new power line but there is nothing left of it. In February 2022, Eskom switched off the line to perform maintenance. That same day, the cable thieves struck. The main artery of the line was cut and the line was never switched on again. It has taken the criminals seven months to steal 60 km of the line. Now, they are returning to remove the steel from what is left of the structures. While this was happening, Martie called out for help to the authorities multiple times. The Police did nothing and private security could not do much to assist the land owners in protecting them, their land or Eskom’s infrastructure. a Network of farmers was formed and 13 cable thieves were arrested in March, only to be released from custody three days later. All 13 criminals struck again. Desperate for help, Martie wrote to Andre De Ruyter. And Andre phoned her, spending two hours on the phone to gather information. 50 Security vehicles were deployed to the area at a monthly cost of over 500 million Rand. But it didn’t help. Patrolling on farms is a different story than patrolling in the city. Eskom later said, the security bill was too high and withdrew the vehicles, leaving only three to patrol the 80km line. De Ruyter instructed high level meetings between local Eskom management and farmers at the Kusile power station. Ideas were exchanged and Eskom undertook to work with the farmers and private security to protect the line. But that was the last of it. Eskom never responded to reports again. And it seems that there could be a leak between Eskom and the criminals, because they know all too well that nothing is being done. The ripple effect of this problem is massive. Farmers are too scared to work their land because strangers are constantly moving in and out of their gates. When they are cut cables exceeding 100 meters and massively heavy are dropped onto the farm land making it impossible for farmers to work their land. And Eskom never comes out to collect the cables. Despite more attempts made to get Eskom to respond, again, directly to Andre De Ruyter seem to have fallen on death ears. Treatment idea: - It is Friday night and Martie and her children are having dinner in their house. We hear the two way radio alerts come through.. Martie tells her children to get ready for the night, they check all the doors and windows… in the passage, our presenter introducing the night on the farm… - Then we take a trip with Martie to the hotspots and see what we can find. - The next day we visit the same hotspots and go to the place where the first cable was chopped in March. - We visit the local Eskom office, where no one is working from their offices… - We speak to Eskom, preferably ADR. Who is responsible here? - Energy expert: explanatory: just how much is 400KVA? Is this problem contributing to loadshedding in the city? Additional elements: • Land owners also suffer massive losses as the criminals’ open access to the farms lead to extended crimes: they steal anything they can find while making their way to the power line: they steal solar systems, pumps, vehicles ect. • Baldwin is planning on building 600 thousand cost low income houses on land in the middle of this mess. The Vulcan line was supposed to supply power to this development. • The Maputo corridor, which is under construction, is also supposed to get power supply from the Vulcan line.
